artists.biography: Nadia Reid (born Nadia Reid-O’Reilly on 23 August 1991) is a New Zealand singer-songwriter based in Auckland. Her albums, "Listen to Formation, Look for the Signs", and "Preservation", have received wide acclaim at home in New Zealand and internationally. Reid performs live with a regular band of musicians consisting of Sam Taylor (guitar), Richie Pickard (bass), and Joe McCallum (drums). Reid’s first single from her album ‘’Preservation’’, "Richard", saw her nominated for the APRA Silver Scroll award in 2017, regarded as New Zealand’s most important songwriting award. Reid herself was nominated for Best Solo Artist, Breakthrough Artist of the Year and Best Alternative Artist. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Listen to Formation, Look for the Signs is the debut full-length album by New Zealand singer-songwriter Nadia Reid, originally released in 2014. The album blends elements of folk, pop, country, and world music, showcasing Reid's clear, confident vocal delivery paired with introspective and poetic songwriting. Recorded in Lyttelton, New Zealand, and produced by Ben Edwards, the album features a sparse, intimate musical style that highlights Reid's lyrical depth and emotional nuance.

This album marked a significant entry in Reid's discography, following her earlier EP Letters I Wrote And Never Sent, and established her as a distinctive voice in contemporary folk and singer-songwriter circles. Critics praised the album for its mature songwriting and Reid's assured performance, drawing comparisons to artists like Laura Marling. It received strong acclaim from publications such as Mojo, Uncut, and The Guardian, which highlighted its soulful and self-possessed qualities. The album's thoughtful exploration of themes like loss and resilience resonated with listeners, earning it a respected place in the folk and indie music scenes.
